_doc: Next.js findings generalised from real autonomous runs: verification by full production build, cold caches after wiping .next, heap exhaustion, repeated dev-server restarts, jobs competing for the same CPU. Fields: detector.regex runs on sanitized Bash commands (or tool results when match_target=result); evidence = thresholds that must be met; estimate = stated arithmetic inputs.

rules.title: Full `next build` used as a quick correctness check

estimate.assumption: an incremental `tsc --noEmit` plus lint answers 'does it compile' in roughly 20-35% of a production build; keep one full build per ship

rules.why: A production build compiles, bundles, optimises and prerenders everything. For 'did my edit break types or imports' it does far more work than needed, and it is run again and again.
rules.fix: Verify with an incremental typecheck and lint; run the full build only once before shipping or when build-only behaviour (routes, prerender, env) changed.
rules.before: npm run build   # after every small edit
rules.after: npx tsc --noEmit --incremental && npx next lint   # full `next build` once, at the end

rules.title: `.next` deleted before building, so every build is cold

estimate.assumption: a warm .next cache makes the following build or dev start about 40% faster; stale-cache bugs are the exception, not the routine

rules.why: Wiping the cache is a reflex against stale output, but it throws away incremental compilation work every time.
rules.fix: Delete .next only when a build is demonstrably stale (config, env or dependency change). Otherwise keep it, and keep it per worktree.
rules.after: npm run build   # rm -rf .next only after next.config / dependency changes

rules.title: Next.js run with webpack explicitly

estimate.assumption: Turbopack is typically 2-5x faster for dev start and incremental rebuilds; 0.4 is conservative

rules.why: Webpack was chosen on purpose, yet the commands are slow enough to matter.
rules.fix: Try Turbopack (`--turbopack`, default in recent Next versions) unless a plugin requires webpack.

rules.title: Next.js dev/build without Turbopack

estimate.assumption: only applies to Next versions where Turbopack is opt-in; ignore on versions where it is the default

rules.why: On Next versions before Turbopack became the default, dev and build use webpack unless asked otherwise.
rules.fix: Check the Next version. If it is older than the Turbopack-default release, add --turbopack to dev (and build where supported).

rules.title: Build or dev crashed on Node heap exhaustion

detector.regex: JavaScript heap out of memory|FATAL ERROR: .*(Reached heap limit|heap)|ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY

estimate.assumption: the crashed run is pure waste; a larger heap or fewer parallel jobs avoids the rerun

rules.why: The default Node heap is too small for the build, or several heavy jobs share the machine; the run dies and gets repeated.
rules.fix: Set NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=<MB> sized to free RAM, and do not start two heavy builds side by side.

rules.title: Dev server started repeatedly

estimate.assumption: each start costs about 20 s of cold compile plus at least one turn to check it is up; keeping one server alive saves all but the first

rules.why: Hot reload makes restarts unnecessary; each restart repeats cold compilation and the agent turns spent on checking readiness.
rules.fix: Start one dev server in the background per worktree, reuse it for curl/browser checks, restart only after config/env/dependency changes.
rules.before: pkill -f next; npm run dev &   # before each check
rules.after: npm run dev > /tmp/dev.log 2>&1 &   # once; then curl localhost:3000

rules.title: Dependencies reinstalled again and again (worktrees, fresh clones)

estimate.assumption: a shared content-addressed store (pnpm) or --prefer-offline cache cuts repeat installs by about 60%

rules.why: Every worktree or clean checkout pays a full install and stores a full copy of node_modules (also a disk problem).
rules.fix: Use pnpm with a shared store (hard links), or npm --prefer-offline, and only reinstall when the lockfile changed.

rules.title: Heavy jobs overlapped on one machine

estimate.assumption: overlapping CPU-bound jobs each run slower than alone; serialising or capping workers recovers about a quarter of the overlapped time. Inferred from tool timing only

rules.why: Two or more heavy commands (often from parallel agents) ran at the same time. Their durations are inflated by contention, and memory kills become more likely.
rules.fix: Serialise heavy jobs with a lock (flock) or a small job queue, and cap workers per job.
rules.before: agent A: next build   |   agent B: next build   (simultaneously)
rules.after: flock /tmp/heavy.lock next build   # one heavy job at a time
